Javad Qarai, a documentary filmmaker and nature enthusiast, posted a video on his Instagram account on Monday, 27 Mehr, showing the rescue operation for Iranian fighter jet pilots after they crashed during the 40-day war. He says he beeped over the pilot's voice to keep him unidentified. This documentary filmmaker says he went with a helicopter and several people to the central Alborz mountains to rescue two "Yak-130" fighter jet pilots who were targeted in an Israeli attack on 13 Esfand 1404. He stated the rescue area as "Afjeh to Dasht-e Lar." The Iranian "Yak-130" fighter jet, which had taken off to counter Israeli F-35s, was targeted and its pilots ejected and landed in the Lavasan mountains. The Israeli Defense Forces published the news and video of this incident on 13 and 14 Esfand 1404.radiofarda@mamlekate

📝 A grounded aviation fleet and long, costly journeys for IraniansThe CEO of the Islamic Republic of Iran Airlines has reported the destruction of 30 to 40 aircraft in the recent war and a sharp drop in Homa's fleet capacity. These remarks come as foreign routes grow more restricted, parts procurement becomes more difficult, and Iranians' overseas travel is disrupted—all while US sanctions on airlines and their service providers, together with war damage, accumulated debts, and management problems, have plunged Iran's aviation industry into a wide-ranging crisis.Taher Abdolhayi, CEO of Iran Air, says Iran needs roughly a thousand aircraft, but of the more than 300 it has, only 130 to 140 were flying—and of those, 30 to 40 were destroyed in the war. He put the total number of aircraft targeted in the war at 70 to 80, and describing the destruction of one of Homa's planes, he said the company's aircraft was "pulverized" by a missile strike in the recent war.@mamlekate
